manifest.title: SentinelTrack P11.5 Evidence Report
manifest.description: Technical evidence pack for the isolated SentinelTrack P11.5 dataset audit and measured baselines.

charts.title: Audited image records by source
charts.subtitle: Source-equivalent copies are retained for audit and excluded from V2 mixing.

blocks.body:
## Technical Summary

The strongest measured result is the existing P3 plate detector at **0.8547 F1** on the locked detector test. The selected PP-OCRv5 mobile recognizer reaches **0.5787 exact match** on the locked OCR test and is materially faster than the server alternative.

The audit also finds substantial source duplication: **3,531 exact-duplicate groups containing 9,593 records**. The isolated V2 derivative removes exact copies and preserves identity/sequence separation. P11.5 remains open because P1 accuracy, model tournaments, fine-tuning, temporal fusion, full end-to-end performance, cloud profiles, and multi-stream capacity do not yet have the required evidence.

Evidence files: `reports/p11_5/baseline/p3_baseline.json`, `reports/p11_5/baseline/p4_baseline.json`, and `reports/p11_5/dataset/audit_summary.json`.

## The audit supports controlled derivative training

The inventory has **13,081 image records plus one orphan XML record**. Sixty-two images have no label, and 137 records carry quality or quarantine flags. The canonical frozen split has zero cross-split exact-image duplicates, and the legacy OCR identity audit has zero train/validation/test overlaps.

| Finding | Evidence | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| Exact duplicate groups | 3,531 groups / 9,593 records | Deduplicate before mixing sources |
| Near-duplicate candidates | 3,514 groups | Review before treating as independent evidence |
| Unlabeled images | 62 | Exclude until labels are supplied |
| Detection V2 | 5,281 unique images | Derivative-ready, not trained |
| OCR V2 | 1,396 train / 150 expanded val / 178 locked test | Historical test preserved, not trained |

The implication is practical: the existing canonical corpora can remain locked while V2 incorporates validated raw sources under deterministic hash, identity, and sequence grouping.

## Definitions and method

The audit grain is one image/annotation record, with explicit orphan records. Exact duplicates use SHA-256; near-duplicate candidates use perceptual-hash distance. Detection labels are validated for class, normalized coordinates, and box geometry. OCR identity grouping uses the available parent identity/text metadata. Detection V2 excludes source-equivalent copies, preserves canonical splits, and converts validated VOC/polygon annotations to class-0 boxes without rewriting source annotations.

P3 metrics are precision, recall, and F1 from the locked 167-image test split with 169 annotated plates. OCR exact match is the fraction of labelled crops whose normalized predicted string equals the normalized label; character accuracy and CER are reported in the companion OCR report.

## Limitations and open gates

The workspace has no vehicle-labelled ground-truth corpus, so P1 accuracy and the YOLO11-versus-YOLO26 vehicle tournament are not evaluated. OBB and OCR V2 data are derivative-ready but untrained. Video frames are sequence-capable, but there is no locked frame-level OCR track for temporal evaluation. A local single-frame detector probe cannot establish safe camera capacity, and cloud profiles have no benchmarked artifacts. Unknown or unverified source licensing also limits public-submission readiness.

## Recommended next steps

1. Obtain or create a legitimate vehicle-labelled locked benchmark with scene, camera, and time-based grouping.
2. Train the V2 and OBB derivatives, then compare challengers on fixed splits with measured VRAM and latency.
3. Fine-tune OCR V2 only after validating label provenance and preserving the historical locked test.
4. Create a frame-level OCR track protocol and measure single-frame versus temporal policies.
5. Run full end-to-end and multi-stream tests on the target server before promoting any profile.
